score_note: REV is NS because current comparable organic expansion cannot be established. No missing factor is replaced by 5 or reweighted. gates.reason: Related-party acquisition/loans and legacy compliance matters require scrutiny; approval safeguards, disclosed responses and unmodified opinions are counter-evidence. No evidenced severe integrity abuse established.

Audited statements support historical facts and claim mapping. Current acquisition-perimeter cash classification, organic revenue and entity allocations remain unresolved; they block specific factors/point valuation, not every historical conclusion. June reclassification of other income and expense does not alter profit.

Base cash path survives without rescue. Restrained no-rescue stress has a modeled gap while a collection countercase survives; precise lien release, current cash and entity fungibility are not verified. Hypothetical rescue neither proves a pass nor a modeled gap establishes an actual default.

Official turnover supports a coarse 5–10-day reference exit but lots, sparse latest trading and next-session cautions constrain implementation. No suspension inferred from status code 6; live depth/spread unavailable.

sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Fidel is an established bilingual IT and language-services business with a genuine Japan–India delivery niche, but the current investment case is an acquisition-integration case rather than a demonstrated organic compounder. Group FY2026 revenue reached ₹102.36 crore and owner PAT ₹13.81 crore. Those figures combine three acquired businesses with a changing parent/subsidiary delivery mix. June-quarter owner PAT subsequently fell 15.20% while reported revenue rose 127.98%. The economic question is whether acquired onshore relationships can produce durable, cash-backed per-share growth, not whether reported consolidated sales can double. [S1, S2, S6, S7]

Verdict: Hold for evidence / acquisition-integration watchlist. BQS, GQS and IAS are NS, with non-renormalized BQS bounds 4.70–5.78 and GQS bounds 3.60–7.20. REV is specifically unscoreable because current organic comparability is missing; several other factors are scoreable at mixed/adequate levels. A conditional base case produces 16.55% nominal pretax five-year XIRR at ₹170, but that is not a defensible point target while current cash, legal-entity fungibility and IM minority-value allocation remain unverified. A higher computed return is not permission to waive missing evidence. [S1–S8]

The three decisive positives are historical client delivery, established Japanese local access, and low-coupon amortizing debt with a funded base model. The three decisive risks are acquisition-led rather than proven organic growth, weaker post-acquisition margins, and financial assets that cannot all be treated as unrestricted cash. No severe integrity abuse or actual default is established by the reviewed evidence. [S1, S2, S7–S10]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Cutoff: 20 October 2026. Last market session: 19 October because 20 October is a market holiday. NSE SME FIDEL, ISIN INE0LQQ01019, close ₹170; 13,750,560 current issued shares imply ₹233.76 crore market capitalization. The September pattern declares no outstanding warrants, convertibles or ESOPs. Board lot is 1,000 shares, about ₹1.70 lakh at the close. Price is historical, not an executable bid or offer. [S8, S18, S21]

Four gates: G1 Conditional, G2 Conditional, G3 Hold—unresolved, G4 Conditional. G1 retains related-party scrutiny and disclosed responses without an abuse finding. G2 distinguishes reliable reported statements from an incomplete acquired-cash/organic-growth bridge. G3 is unresolved because base and a collection countercase survive while a slower-collection restrained case does not, and current legally available cash is unverified. G4 is not a suspension finding: eligible SM status code 6 means price discovery. [S1, S2, S7, S19–S22]

Reported annual financial history and identity are High confidence. Governance, cash interpretation, operating capability and coarse liquidity are Medium. Current organic revenue, current available cash and minority terminal attribution are Low. Low material factors remain NS; historical input confidence is not inflated merely because a forecast is plausible. No proposed position, risk tolerance or portfolio exposure was supplied, so ₹5 lakh and a 15% nominal pretax equity hurdle are analytical reference assumptions only.

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors: GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV NS, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 5, BAL 5, EXEC 6, EARN 5. IAS inputs: Q NS because final BQS is NS; R NS; D 4; P NS; L 3. Factor-level facts, counter-evidence, subject-specific confidence and evidence IDs are retained in the audit. Scores are not neutral placeholders: the 5s describe evidenced mixed economics, while missing comparable growth and value inputs remain explicitly missing.

BQS known weighted contribution is 4.58 at 88% coverage; REV's 12% missing weight yields a possible 4.70–5.78, not a new point score. GQS known contribution is 3.20 at 60% coverage, yielding 3.60–7.20. IAS known contribution is 1.10 at 30% coverage, yielding broad mechanical bounds 1.80–8.10. Missing weights are never redistributed. These intervals are algebraic evidence bounds, not probabilistic forecasts or ranking scores.

No G1-failure, G3-failure, persistent CAP≤3 or persistent CASH≤3 override is applied. A conditional financing rescue does not clear G3; an unresolved gate does not justify inventing a numeric cap. No historical score of 9–10 is claimed. Full-precision arithmetic is retained; presentation may use half-up one-decimal rounding. All three aggregates are excluded from numeric rankings until their missing factors can be established.

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text:
Fidel supplies bilingual technology consulting, digital engineering, localization, language/data services and staffing/managed-service delivery. Its practical niche is helping Japanese and other international customers use Indian technology talent while maintaining local-language support. Management describes technology/bilingual consulting and digital engineering as approximately 70% of revenue and language/data engineering as about 30%. This is an attributed mix, not an audited product-segment breakout. The audited accounts report one operating segment and ₹97.53 crore of ₹102.36 crore FY2026 revenue from customers outside India. Overseas subsidiaries can have local “domestic” revenue; that accounting label does not mean all such sales are India sales. [S1, S6]

The group perimeter matters: the Indian parent owns FidelSoft Inc. and Fidel Technologies KK; Techvine is a wholly owned US step-down subsidiary, and IM Corporation is 83%-owned through Japan. Financial notes consolidate Fidel Technologies from 12 June 2025, Techvine from 1 August and IM from 6 January 2026. Board/acquisition documents also contain other closing/transaction dates. These need a control-versus-closing reconciliation, not a presumption of wrongdoing. The remaining 17% of IM belongs to minority owners, not the entire group's public shareholders. [S1, S11, S24]

Revenue is earned from people, technical delivery, projects and recurring managed services rather than a disclosed high-margin software subscription base. Product initiatives such as Spoggle and FIX-related tools may add differentiation, but current evidence does not support valuing all revenue like proprietary SaaS. Cash wages, subcontractors, collection timing and client renewal are the important unit-economic constraints. [S6, S7]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The strongest evidence of differentiation is the combination of local Japanese delivery, bilingual engineering and long-lived India–Japan relationships. Management reports more than 150 delivery personnel in Japan and describes customers requiring Japanese first-line support, with offshore work potentially following. The commenced JPY100 million annual managed-services engagement and Japan Capability Center initiative are concrete access points. CMMI Level 3 is a reported process milestone that may help procurement qualification. None is proof of monopoly pricing or an unassailable moat. [S6, S7, S14, S23]

Counter-evidence is meaningful: management says roughly 70% of business comes through systems integrators/partners; project staffing and language work have many substitutes; customer concentration, renewal cohorts and price realization are not fully quantified. Generative AI can expand data-validation/engineering work but also compress routine translation prices. Local language competence creates friction, not automatic switching costs equivalent to mission-critical software lock-in. [S6, S7]

MOAT 5 reflects useful but contestable positioning. Large Indian IT service companies are contextual delivery competitors, not clean valuation comparables for this small acquired group. Japanese staffing/consulting firms may resemble onshore cost economics but differ in capital structure and disclosure. No borrowed peer multiple is presented as evidence; the 6×/9×/12× scenario EV/EBITDA multiples are declared analyst assumptions.

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The reliable parent history is ₹22.38/25.71/26.31/33.37/40.09/54.81 crore revenue in FY2020–FY2025. That gives a five-year CAGR of 19.62% from ₹22.3757 to ₹54.8054 crore and a three-year FY2022–FY2025 CAGR of 27.71% from ₹26.3131 to ₹54.8054 crore. This history is useful, but selecting only that endpoint to score current growth would avoid the latest structural change. The nominal FY2021–FY2026 parent CAGR is 13.76%; it is not a clean organic measure after customer migration. Ten-year comparable CAGR is NA, not invented. [S1, S3–S5]

FY2026 group revenue increased ₹47.32 crore, or 85.96%, to ₹102.36 crore. Parent revenue fell ₹5.81 crore, or -10.60%. Management explains that some clients moved to onshore delivery within the new US/Japan structure. This makes both a simple “86% organic growth” assertion and a simple “10.6% underlying demand collapse” assertion unsound. Acquisitions entered at different dates, and no full current constant-perimeter revenue bridge was established from the annuals, prospectus, acquisition notices or calls. REV is NS rather than a favorable stale-period score. [S1, S3, S7, S11]

June 2026 group revenue was ₹37.9323 crore versus ₹16.6381 crore, up 127.98%; owner PAT fell from ₹3.6338 to ₹3.0814 crore. Reported-perimeter TTM sales are ₹123.6528 crore and owner PAT ₹13.2565 crore. These are mechanical FY2026 plus June 2026 minus June 2025 calculations, not organic TTM growth or a promise of current run rate. Parent June sales were ₹10.8534 crore versus ₹14.7579 crore and PAT ₹1.7414 crore versus ₹3.3118 crore; these weaker parent figures are retained, not hidden, but customer migration also prevents interpreting them as pure lost group demand. Q4 revenue of ₹37.27 crore and June ₹37.93 suggest an acquired quarterly scale around ₹150 crore annualized, subject to seasonality and integration. [S1, S2]

Management's ₹100-to-₹500 crore five-year vision and ₹300 crore intermediate ambition are explicitly not formal annual guidance. A JPY100 million annual order, a roughly ₹10 crore Hyderabad annualized base, ₹20 lakh Spoggle projects and approximately ₹1 crore JCC scope help ground opportunity but do not add up to contracted ₹500 crore backlog. [S6, S7, S23]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
FY2026 acquisitions broadened geography and customer access but brought goodwill of ₹18.5684 crore, overseas borrowing, different labor economics and inherited advances. Management describes 53% of revenue as lower-margin onshore US/Japan work and an 18–24 month period of integration and capability investment. Cross-selling and shifting suitable work offshore are credible levers; neither the speed nor eventual margin is established. DUR 6 and EXEC 6 recognize access and completed milestones while retaining integration risk. [S1, S6, S7]

Reported FY2026 core EBITDA excluding other income is ₹17.1159 crore. Removing the ₹2.1449 crore net FX gain embedded in other expense and expensing ₹1.4795 crore of capitalized product development gives a conservative cash-development/FX-normalized EBITDA diagnostic of ₹13.4915 crore. This is our normalization, not a corrected issuer statement. The later June filing grosses up FY2026 other income and other expense by the same ₹2.1554 crore; PBT is unchanged, so that presentation change is not missing profit. [S1, S2]

Acquisition-inclusive broad capital committed, defined as owner equity plus NCI plus debt less cash, short deposits, MF and unquoted current investments, rose from ₹15.22 to ₹65.01 crore. It deliberately leaves goodwill and risky advances in capital at risk. Normalized current NOPAT is ₹9.46 crore under a 28% tax assumption: about 14.55% on closing broad capital, versus 23.57% on average capital. Partial-year acquired earnings distort both timing measures. The approximately 1.87% acquisition-inclusive incremental ratio is not organic marginal ROIC and cannot prove recurring value destruction. CAP 5 is supported by mixed/unseasoned cohorts, not a false precision claim. The analytical 12–16% capital-cost comparison is an assumption, not a sourced company WACC. [S1, S3, S7]

The forecast funds cash wages/benefits and product-development expense within operating margin, plus at least 1% of annual revenue as maintenance/technology capex, increasing WC, debt service and legacy obligations. No additional acquisitions are essential to the survival cases. The model does not convert a contemplated US$3 million subsidiary authorization into external cash. [S1, S24]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoters held 73.07% at September 2026; the shareholding and annual declaration report nil encumbrance. Parent-disclosed FY2026 remuneration for Sunil and Prachi together was ₹0.7298 crore, about 5.3% of group owner PAT. This is not a full group-pay total: the annual report says the whole-time director also receives remuneration from a subsidiary. Ownership alignment is a positive, not independent assurance about minority treatment. [S1, S8, S17]

The Japanese acquisition was a related-party purchase. April 2025 approval materials described 388 shares and an up-to-₹6.5 crore consideration, with promoters excluded from voting; the annual RPT note records ₹6.8219 crore paid to the promoter, while board narrative uses another rupee acquisition figure. The documents reviewed do not supply a complete consideration/FX/transaction-cost bridge. That is a reconciliation question and valuation issue, not evidence by itself of an unauthorized payment. Related operating transactions and the LinguaSol loan merit ongoing scrutiny; authorized RPT ceilings are not realized revenue or evidence of diversion. [S1, S9, S10]

The FY2026 secretarial report describes a historic 2007 overseas-allotment FC-GPR matter, a July 2025 compounding application and its September 2025 return by RBI. The board says it is evaluating options and working with its bank. A ₹10,000 voting-results-format fine is described as paid in the secretarial report and payment initiated in the board response; exact completion is not independently verified. A January professional-tax disclosure describes ₹6,406 total dues including a ₹283 penalty and says the amount was paid. These are scoped disclosure facts, not a broad integrity or solvency finding. [S1, S12]

The July EPS clarification says a September 2025 value was omitted in XBRL while the signed PDF disclosed EPS ₹4.66 correctly; no change to the other financial values was claimed. Annual opinions were unmodified. June review relied on other auditors for three foreign entities and did not qualify its conclusion for that reliance. Completed acquisitions and commencement of managed services are positive execution facts; management's admitted integration period and margin pressure are contrary facts. GOV 5 and EXEC 6 retain both sides. [S1, S2, S6, S7, S13, S14]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Earnings-to-cash: FY2026 group PBT ₹18.3198 crore reconciles through DA, interest, nonoperating gains and FX to pre-WC operating cash ₹16.4390 crore. Receivables absorbed ₹10.7742 crore and other current assets ₹5.7891 crore; payables, other current liabilities and provisions provided offsets. Tax paid was ₹4.1906 crore and reported CFO ₹7.7323 crore, only 55.03% of group PAT. Parent CFO was ₹10.8216 crore against ₹9.3036 crore PAT; FY2022–FY2026 cumulative parent conversion is 64.02%. The latest parent release is helpful but does not erase earlier weak conversion. [S1, S3–S5]

Acquired balances are the principal cash-interpretation issue. The group cash statement records ₹42.8676 crore borrowing inflow, equal to closing debt; management explicitly says IM brought pre-existing debt. The ₹9.4490 crore PPE cash line is also not simply the ₹3.1501 crore gross asset additions: the fixed-asset note separately includes ₹6.9346 crore acquired gross assets and transfers. A full acquisition cash-flow bridge is therefore needed before calling the reported group FCF organic. This is a two-sided classification/perimeter caveat, not an assertion of unaccounted cash. Closing audited cash still reconciles: ₹7.2043 + ₹3.2160 = ₹10.4203 crore. [S1, S7]

At March, reported good net receivables were ₹26.9332 crore; doubtful ₹0.1688 crore was already fully provided and is not written off again in the model. Good balances over three years were ₹0.8266 crore, close to the separately disclosed LinguaSol trade balance ₹0.8267 crore. That trade balance is distinct from its ₹2.7096 crore loan. The company reports ₹0.80 crore annual principal receipts and a ₹0.20 crore quarterly schedule to FY2030, supported by a personal guarantee and management turnaround expectations; receipt evidence and future repayment remain different things. Noninterest foreign advances of ₹16.3093 crore are not treated as spendable liquidity. [S1, S7]

The opening-claim ledger maps 42 balances/treatments. Operating WC is ₹21.0363 crore, including tax-authority balances, prepayments, employee/supplier advances, all ordinary payables and accruals. Net tax ₹0.9455 crore is paid separately; March advance-tax/TDS asset is zero. Old dividend ₹0.0328 crore is matched to dividend-account cash once. Current benefits ₹0.5746 crore and noncurrent legacy benefits ₹5.3219 crore are scheduled separately from new service costs. A ₹0.0911 crore benefit-table reconciliation difference is retained as a limitation; the higher balance-sheet liability controls the model. Future ordinary benefit funding does not erase the legacy balance. [S1]

Cash equivalents include restricted/dividend and possibly earmarked pools. The model conservatively places ₹1.3268 crore unspent IPO WC money inside, not in addition to, opening cash; it is spent only against authorized incremental WC. ₹21.049 crore MF book value is not treated as free funding because loans are lien-secured; exact pledged amount remains unknown. Term deposits mature on explicit assumed dates, tested with no cash release. ₹42.8676 crore debt, ₹7.4877 crore current maturities, ordinary operating rent, remaining deposits and goodwill are all treated consistently: operating leases stay in expense, goodwill gets no independent terminal cash value, and acquired deals are not paid a second time. [S1, S15]

Debt coupons are low but currency is not risk-free. Parent yen facilities are disclosed at 3.65%, with five-year schedules; other foreign debt spans shorter and 1–10-year terms. Japanese revenues provide a possible natural economic hedge, not proof that every loan, cash pool and cost is perfectly matched. Rates +200bp, accelerated foreign maturity, noncollection, MF-value and minority-allocation sensitivities are shown. No undisclosed committed facility is assumed. [S1, S7]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹170, market capitalization is ₹233.7595 crore, about 17.63× reported-perimeter TTM owner profit and 4.18× parent-shareholder book equity. Neither is a reliable stand-alone valuation conclusion: TTM has changing acquisitions, financial assets include liens/uncertain recoveries, and NCI is an economic claim. A five-year cash/debt/tax/WC model is used instead, dated from 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, with a March-to-entry cash bridge and June P&L anchor. [S1, S2, S8, S18]

Bear assumptions: revenue ₹145 crore FY2027 to ₹185 crore terminal run rate, about 10–10.5% cash EBITDA margin, 21–22% WC/revenue, 6× exit EBITDA, partial related-loan and MF recovery, and no future discretionary dividend. Without rescue the path is unfunded, with a maximum running gap ₹3.32 crore, so no shareholder IRR is shown for that path. A separate hypothetical rescue facility of ₹9.15 crore at 12% funds the modeled path and produces ₹94.90 terminal price and -11.01% XIRR. That facility is not verified as available. [S1, S2; analyst assumptions]

Base: ₹155/185/220/260/300 crore FY2027–FY2031 revenue and ₹335 crore terminal run rate, cash EBITDA margin rising 12.5% to 14.5%, 16% WC/revenue, funded capex at least 1% of sales and 9× exit EBITDA. No new debt or equity is needed in this conditional group pool; minimum cash is ₹6.00 crore. Terminal EV ₹437.17 plus cash and selected financial assets, less debt/legacy claims and ₹20.27 IM minority value, gives common equity ₹477.78 crore, ₹347.46 per share and 16.55% XIRR including cash-reducing future dividends. No pre-entry dividend is credited to the investor. [S1, S2, S15, S16; analyst assumptions]

Bull: revenue ₹165 crore FY2027 to ₹550 crore terminal run rate, cash margin rising to 17%, 15% WC/revenue and 12× exit EBITDA. The conditional path is internally funded and yields ₹857.59 per share and 39.52% XIRR. It requires successful integration, offshore economics and continued client expansion; it is not management's promise or a probability-weighted recommendation. Forecasts carry no assigned probabilities. [S6, S7; analyst assumptions]

Minority treatment is explicit: 17% is applied only to modeled IM equity, not to all group equity or to its ₹0.2888 crore book NCI. The model assumes IM has 25% of terminal EBITDA and 20% of residual cash, allocates associated foreign debt/advances, and tests a 40% operating/cash share. Those are clearly conditional allocations, not verified entity forecasts. Current legal cash availability and this allocation uncertainty keep R and P NS, even though scenario math is reproducible.

Reverse hurdle: holding FY2027 at ₹155 crore, the base margin/WC/9× exit framework needs approximately 15.13% annual later growth, reaching ₹313.55 crore terminal sales, for a 15% five-year XIRR. The 12% and 18% hurdles need roughly ₹270.84 and ₹361.20 crore. Margin and terminal-multiple matrices, debt timing, loan recovery, restricted-asset value and legacy funding are all re-solved with cash constraints. Entry-price thresholds are diagnostic only, not buy orders or validated fair values.

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
A plausible loss mechanism is not simply slower translation revenue. Acquired low-margin onshore work can expand sales while weak utilization, wage pressure, product investment and slower collection compress cash. Debt amortization and the already-approved dividend remain obligations even if discretionary acquisitions stop. Foreign advances and pledged MF cannot be assumed to cure an operating cash gap immediately. [S1, S6, S7, S15, S16]

The restrained no-rescue test fixes FY2027 revenue at ₹125 crore, below the acquired roughly ₹150 crore run rate, starts cash EBITDA margin at 8%, assumes 20% WC/revenue and essential capex at least 1% of sales, no additional acquisitions and no related-loan cash recovery. It produces a modeled maximum running shortfall of ₹3.20 crore, first appearing in 2027-02-28. This is an assumption-driven stress path, not evidence of an actual payment failure. [S1, S2, S7; analyst assumptions]

The same restrained operations with WC at 17% rather than 20% survive without rescue, minimum modeled cash ₹0.92 crore, but terminal equity is only ₹72.40 per share and the conditional XIRR -15.70%. The difference is economically material collection timing, not a free rescue. March WC against a partial-year revenue base is not a reliable forward turnover ratio; the June run rate makes the countercase plausible but not verified. G3 therefore remains Hold—unresolved rather than a forced Fail or an invented pass.

A more delayed 27%-initial-WC boundary creates a larger gap, but it is not stacked onto every other remote loss to manufacture a failure. The base sensitivity also gives zero value to inherited advances without simultaneously pretending they were operating cash. Permanent-loss channels include loss of goodwill/inherited financial assets, forced low-price funding, client loss and sustained margin decline. Tax deductions from hypothetical write-offs are not assumed to rescue cash. Precise entity restrictions, collateral release and actual collections would determine whether the credible stress gap can be absorbed.

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Five times sales is not five times shareholder wealth. Management's ₹100-to-₹500 crore vision begins from a partly consolidated FY2026 base and says nothing definitive about future margins, acquisition prices, WC, dilution or exit valuation. All of those must be funded before comparing share outcomes. [S6, S7]

At the base 9× exit EBITDA, terminal 14.5% cash margin and modeled reinvestment/claims, five times total nominal investor wealth requires approximately ₹858.8 crore terminal revenue, or 40.84% annual growth after the ₹155 crore FY2027 assumption. Ten times requires approximately ₹1781.6 crore and 62.97%. The solver reruns WC, capex of at least 1% of sales, taxes, cash, debt and potential dilution; it does not multiply the current P/E blindly. Both mathematical crossings fund within the model, but no evidence establishes enough organic client demand or people-management capacity to deliver them.

The bull scenario reaches approximately fivefold terminal share price only by combining much higher ₹550 crore sales with 17% cash margins and a 12× exit, plus favorable asset recoveries. That confluence is possible as arithmetic, not demonstrated as a likely outcome. A 10× designation is unsupported. Integration milestones and renewed cash-backed owner EPS, rather than a headline acquired-growth percentage, would be the evidence needed to revisit this assessment.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
At the next results review, require a revenue bridge separating acquisition contributions, onshore/offshore customer migration, FX and comparable customer demand. Two comparable half-years or four quarters would be more meaningful than one large acquired-growth quarter. Evidence that margins stabilize while owner EPS and cash collections improve would strengthen REV/EARN; sales growth without those outcomes would not. [S1, S2, S6, S7]

Cash priorities: reconcile the IM acquired balance sheet to actual cash movements; obtain entity cash and collateral schedules; confirm the 1.3268-crore IPO earmark's location/use; reconcile current maturities and the foreign long-debt ladder; verify quarterly LinguaSol principal receipts and aged related trade collections. A sustained gap between owner earnings and cash, increasing older receivables, or recurring new external funding to pay ordinary claims would weaken CASH/BAL. [S1, S15]

Governance priorities: obtain the consideration/FX/fees bridge for the related-party acquisition, latest status of the historic FC-GPR matter and documentary closure of the small fine. Preserve the company's response and scale when evaluating any update. No outreach, complaint or regulatory inference is implied by these questions. [S1, S9, S12, S13]

Before any implementation decision, refresh issued shares, price, board lot, live spread/depth and current surveillance status. Recalculate liquidity for the user's actual intended position rather than treating the 5-lakh example as suitable. This is a research checklist, not an active monitoring automation or a promise to trade.

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: Hold for evidence / acquisition-integration watchlist. There is a credible operating franchise and a plausible internally funded base outcome, but no numeric aggregate rank or favorable new-purchase classification is supported while organic-growth and owner-value inputs are incomplete. The framework's compounder designation is not met: MOAT, GOV, CAP and CASH are below the required strength thresholds and REV is NS.

The next decision is evidentiary, not simply a lower price. A cheaper share can improve returns only if the earnings, cash restrictions, minority claim and survival assumptions are reliable. A new-purchase analysis would require the missing acquisition/organic/cash bridge, followed by a re-run of gates, R/P and position-specific tradability. Existing holders would separately weigh verified liquidity and the risk of permanent loss; this dossier does not infer their cost basis, taxes, allocation or constraints.

No trades, portfolio weights, third-party communication, new funding commitments or automatic follow-up were undertaken. Scoring the unknowns as NS is deliberate discipline, not a claim that the company is uninvestable forever.

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary hierarchy: audited issuer annuals and restated IPO statements anchor history; signed exchange/issuer filings anchor acquisitions, shareholding, dividends and regulatory disclosures; NSE dated master/bhavcopy/REG1 files anchor market facts. Management letters/calls provide attributed explanations and intentions, not independent proof. Decisive group balance/P&L/cash-flow, debt, asset-addition and related-party tables and the June P&L were inspected visually. Discovery-only search results and undated intake ratios are not promoted to verified evidence. [S1–S26]

Main analyst assumptions: 28% forward cash tax without an immediate benefit for losses; scenario cash margins including product-development expense; WC ratios; maintenance/technology capex floor; deposit maturity recovery; no operating use of MF collateral; 0/50/100% inherited-advance value; 6×/9×/12× exit EBITDA; 17% IM minority applied to explicitly assumed entity allocations; optional 12% rescue debt and ₹120 equity with 3% fees only after entry. All funding and shareholder returns are conditional on those assumptions. No IRR is assigned to an unfunded path.

Material unresolved questions: current constant-perimeter sales; actual acquired-cash bridge; precise lien/earmark and legal-entity cash restrictions; inherited-advance counterparties/recovery; foreign maturity schedule; acquisition consideration/cost/date reconciliation; and exact current status of the older compliance matter. Small rounding or two-sided presentation differences are not evidence of missing cash. These gaps explain specific NS factors and conditional gates rather than being concealed inside a spurious valuation discount.

The source ledger, factor audit, historical calculations, 42-item claim treatment, annual model summaries and dated return/funding sensitivities preserve the chain from evidence to conclusion. Research cutoff is fixed at 20 October 2026; later snippets or unverified Q2 references are excluded.

sources.title: Fidel FY2026 annual report and audited financial statements

GOV.reason: Promoter holding 73.07%, nil reported pledge and an acquisition approval process with promoter abstention are positives. Related loans, promoter acquisition and unreconciled consideration/cost presentation require scrutiny. Unmodified opinions and minor resolved matters counter a severe-integrity conclusion; no allegation of abuse established.

MOAT.reason: Two-decade Japan–India bilingual delivery and local client access are useful differentiated capabilities. Around 70% partner/system-integrator sourcing, project staffing competition and AI translation commoditization limit demonstrated pricing power; CMMI is a process credential, not exclusivity.

REV.reason: FY2020–FY2025 parent CAGR and FY2022–FY2025 CAGR are measurable, but FY2026 acquisitions and customer migration obscure comparable current organic demand. Neither 86% group growth nor the 10.6% parent decline is a defensible organic score. Alternate annuals, prospectus, target disclosures and management explanations do not supply a current constant-perimeter bridge; REV NS.

DUR.reason: Managed services commenced, Japan delivery footprint and GCC/data-engineering cross-selling provide several accessible avenues. Latest profits and management’s 18–24 month integration focus constrain the pace; early AI pilots and a 500-crore vision are not proven recurring demand.

CAP.reason: Legacy asset-light operations are profitable, but acquisition-inclusive invested capital rose sharply and current normalized return is around a 12–16% analytical capital-cost band rather than demonstrably exceptional. Partial-year acquired earnings, inherited advances and goodwill make organic incremental ROIC NM; no persistent value-destruction conclusion from one transition year.

CASH.reason: Five-year FY2022–FY2026 parent CFO/PAT is about 0.64, with weak early conversion and strong FY2025–FY2026 recovery. Latest parent CFO 10.82 exceeds PAT 9.30, but group reported CFO/PAT is about 0.55 and acquisition cash classifications/aged related balances prevent calling conversion consistently strong. Mixed history supports 5, not fabricated neutral scoring.

BAL.reason: Low-coupon amortizing yen debt and a funded base case are positives. Debt 42.87 crore, liens, inherited advances and collection-dependent survival cases limit flexibility. No assumed rescue is treated as committed and no actual default is inferred.

EXEC.reason: Completed overseas acquisitions, FY2026 scale and commencement of disclosed managed services show delivery. Ongoing integration, margin compression and short evidence on post-acquisition cohorts prevent a higher score; current vision is not a missed hard commitment.

EARN.reason: Owner PAT increased FY2026, but foreign-exchange gains, investment income, capitalized product development and acquisitions materially affect quality/comparability. June owner profit fell 15.2% despite revenue growth; recurring per-share improvement is not yet sustained.

Q.reason: Final BQS is NS because REV is NS; Q uses that exact final result, not a renormalized known-factor average.

R.reason: Conditional funded diagnostics can be calculated, but current legal-entity cash and IM cash/debt/value attribution are not verified closely enough for a defensible scored return spread.

D.reason: A restrained funded collection countercase still implies substantial permanent equity loss, and slower collection creates an unfunded bridge. Positive base cash and low coupons are the counter-evidence; this is modeled risk, not an actual failure finding.

P.reason: The market price is verified, but a robust fair-value range depends on unverified foreign advances, current cash and minority allocation. A numerical scenario range is not sufficient evidence for a scored margin of safety.

L.reason: Observed and conservative missing-session bounds both imply 5–10 days at 5% participation, starting score 5. A 1,000-share lot worth 170,000 rupees, one-trade latest session and concentration/irregular-trading cautions justify a two-point downgrade. Unknown live book is disclosed, not automatically NS.
